source_text: Iustius admoneretur ab his, quos emendare studebat, ut, quantum imperaret, expenderet et sciret primum esse consilii constantis gradum imperii modum tenere; exauctorata quippe doctrina est, quam non tuetur aequitas, et plena auctoritatis, quam iustitiae libra commendat. Ac per hoc constat Apostolum, reverendum ecclesiarum informatorem, rationem magisterii sui consilio aequitate humanitate reddentem nihil de naturali sensisse peccato, sed inculcasse, ut res erat, et vitiorum nos servos nonnisi per voluntatem fuisse et iustitiae nos eadem posse, si corrigatur, voluntate servire. Verum quoniam in expositione loci huius fui hactenus occupatus, ut ostenderem per apostoli Pauli verba Manichaeos nihil posse defendi, patuitque contextu orationis eius veritas, quam per omne dictorum suorum corpus exsequitur, hic sit secundi finis libelli, quo tamen necessario commonemus nihil Traducianis praeter impudentiam remansisse, quia, cum se confiterentur nullum in ratione habere praesidium, de Apostoli dictis, quae exposita sunt, totum sibi solacium vindicabant; et quoniam claruit nihil in his deforme, nihil non sanctitati et rationi consentiens fuisse praescriptum, apparet cecidisse sententiam, quam et ratio cum multis auctoritatibus Scripturarum et, quae in Deo est, religio catholicorum proruit et iam loci istius opinio non tuetur.
pass_a_gloss: He would more justly be warned by those whom he was striving to amend, that he weigh how much he commanded and know that the first step of a constant counsel is to hold a measure of command; for a doctrine is cashiered which equity does not guard, and full of authority which the balance of justice commends. And through this it stands that the Apostle, the reverend informer of the churches, rendering an account of his teaching-office by counsel, equity, humanity, meant nothing about a natural sin, but stamped in, as the matter was, both that we were slaves of vices only through will and that we can, if it is corrected, serve justice by the same will. But since I have until now been occupied in the exposition of this place, so that I might show that through the apostle Paul's words the Manichaeans can be defended in nothing, and the truth which he follows through the whole body of his sayings has been opened by the texture of his speech, let this be the end of the second little book, by which nevertheless we necessarily warn that nothing has remained for the Traduciani besides shamelessness, because, when they confessed that they have no protection in reason, they were claiming for themselves the whole solace from the Apostle's sayings which have been explained; and since it has become clear that nothing deformed in these, nothing not consenting with holiness and reason, was prescribed, it appears that the sentence has fallen, which both reason with many authorities of the Scriptures and the religion of catholics which is in God has overthrown, and now the opinion of this place does not guard.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Traduciani=those who teach tradux peccati; not merely traducianism of the soul
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: Those whom he strove to amend would more rightly admonish him to weigh how much he commanded and recognize that the first step of sound counsel is to observe moderation in commands. Teaching is stripped of authority when fairness does not defend it; it is full of authority when justice’s balance commends it. It is therefore established that the apostle, the churches’ revered teacher, giving an account of his teaching through good judgment, fairness, and humanity, meant nothing about natural sin. Rather, he insisted, as was the case, that we had been slaves of vices only through our will, and that through the same will, if corrected, we can serve righteousness. But since I have been occupied this far in explaining this passage, to show that the Manichaeans can find no defense in the apostle Paul’s words, and since the sequence of his discourse has disclosed the truth he follows throughout the entire body of his statements, let this be the end of the second book. Here, however, we must warn that nothing remains for the advocates of inherited sin except shamelessness. They confessed that they had no defense in reason and claimed all their comfort from the apostolic words we have explained. Now that it is clear these prescribe nothing disgraceful, nothing at odds with holiness and reason, their position has plainly fallen. Reason, together with many scriptural authorities, and the catholics’ reverence for God have overthrown it; and the supposed meaning of this passage no longer protects it (compare Romans 6:17–19).

choices.why: Julian's label for teachers of tradux peccati. Keep the polemic name as a description of transmitted sin, not as a theory of the soul's origin.
Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)
